verses.1: And all of Israel gathered together around David, saying, “Behold, your own words and your actions are our proof.”
verses.2: And also, when you were king, you brought back Israel. And God said to you, “You will rule over my people, Israel. You will be the judge over Israel’s people.”
verses.3: And all the elders of Israel came before King Hebron. David made a covenant with them in Hebron before Jehovah. Then he made David king over Israel, according to Jehovah’s command through Samuel.
verses.4: And David and all of Israel went to Jerusalem. There, in Jerusalem, the Israelites settled down.
verses.5: And the people of Yebus said to David, “Do not enter here.” But David gathered his troops and marched towards Zion. Zion is the city of David.
verses.6: And David said, “All those who fight against Yebusi will become leaders. Yob, son of Zeruya, will also become a leader.”
verses.7: And David sat there, and so the city was named after him: David’s City.
verses.8: And the city was built around it, from the outside to the inside. And Yavav will live in the rest of the city.
verses.9: And David went forth, and he became great. And the LORD’s army was with him.
verses.10: And these are the rulers who supported David during his reign over Israel. They all helped him to rule over Israel, as Jehovah commanded.
verses.11: And these are the names of the giants who lived with David. They were seven in number. They were the leaders of the three tribes. They caused chaos in three parts of the sky at one time.
verses.12: And after him was Elazar, son of Dodo. He was one of the three high priests.
verses.13: It was there that David stood against the Philistines. The Philistines gathered there to fight. It became a battlefield filled with trenches, and the people escaped from the Philistines.
verses.14: And they stood inside the area, and they saved it. They defeated the Philistines. Thus, Jehovah brought great salvation.
verses.15: And thirty men went down from the hills to David. They went to the cave of Adullam, and to the camp of the Philistines, which was located at Rephaim.
verses.16: And David was then in Mizpah, and the Philistines were also there in the house of Lahmam.
verses.17: And David went out and said, “Who will wash me with water from the well that is in the courtyard of the house of bread?”
verses.18: And the three of them were caught in the Philistine camp. Water was drawn from the well where the bread was stored. They brought that water to David, but David did not let them drink it. Instead, he ordered that they be given something else to drink instead.
verses.19: And Chalila said to me, “By the gods! These people’s actions have caused this bloodshed. They brought these people into life, but I will not allow them to live anymore. These three rulers have done this.”
verses.20: And Abshai Ahiyoav was the leader of the three. He was the one who caused his curse to affect three parts of the universe. He had a name among those three.
verses.21: From the three, two were taken captive. They became slaves. And from the three, none came back.
verses.22: Benya, son of Yehoyada, son of Ish-Khayil, a man of great power and ability. He struck two of the Ariel warriors. Then he descended and struck the enemy within the city on the day of snow.
verses.23: And he killed the Egyptian man, a man from Midah. He did this in five minutes. The Egyptian had a chariot with him. He rushed towards him on his chariot, took away the chariot from the Egyptian, and killed him with his own chariot.
verses.24: These were the works of his son, Yehoyada. He had three sons.
verses.25: Of the thirty, he was captured. He didn’t come to the other thirty. David put him to death by hearing.
verses.26: And the officers of the army were appointed by Eliezer, my brother Yoab, from the house of Dodoe.
verses.27: The names of those who are in Hell are Hellez Paloni.
verses.28: Eira ben-Ikesh the Tqoiy, Abiyezr the Anshoyti.
verses.29: My beloved ones, they are my brothers.
verses.30: My beloved, who is covered with skin, is like a white bear in the midst of darkness.
verses.31: Itay ben-Rivai from Gibeath, son of Binyanim, son of Pharaohton.
verses.32: I will bring back from the depths of destruction those who have been lost.
verses.33: The arrogance of those who choose to be proud and self-satisfied.
verses.34: The sons of the name of arrogance are Jonathan, son of Saggeh HaHarrari.
verses.35: Achiam ben Shachar HaHarrimi, Eliphel ben Ur.
verses.36: The Cave of the Merchant, my brother from Phoenicia.
verses.37: The court of the Carmeli youth was full of young men.
verses.38: Come, my brother Nathan, choose a son from the tribe of the foreigners.
verses.39: The Zelek of the Amun people is Nahrayh. He carries all kinds of goods, like those carried by Yovav, son of Tzruya.
verses.42: Adina ben-Shizah Harubeni was the leader of the people. He had thirty followers.
verses.43: Hanan ben-Ma’acha and Yosafat the Judge.
verses.44: Uziyya, I have created her; she shall hear and see the children of Hotham who are in turmoil.
verses.45: Yediel ben Shimri, and his brothers Yochah and Itziy.
verses.46: Eliyel, the warriors and enemies of the people, and Yoshaiah, sons of Elnaam. And Itmah, the leader of the people.
verses.47: Eliyal, and Oved, and Ya’ashiel will create the arrangements.
